# Provenance: the `set_by` ladder

> **Kind:** reference · **Status:** generated

<!-- The table below is generated by tools/gen_provenance_reference.py. -->

<!-- Source: python/glaurung/llm/kb/provenance.py -->

Every writable fact in a `.glaurung` project file — a function name, a
data label, a comment, a stack variable, a type, a prototype — carries a
`set_by` string naming where it came from. That string is ranked, and the
rank decides whether a later write is allowed to replace an earlier one.

## The ladder

12 values across 7 ranks. Values on the same row hold the
same rank on purpose; the gaps between ranks are left free so a new source
can be added without moving an existing one.

| rank | `set_by` | |
|---:|---|---|
| 100 | `manual` | the analyst typed it |
| 80 | `dwarf`, `gopclntab`, `pdb` | the toolchain's own statement about its output |
| 60 | `stdlib` | a curated bundle matched on an exact identifier |
| 50 | `cil`, `flirt` | a signature or metadata match |
| 40 | `ported` | carried from another build of the same function |
| 30 | `propagated` | derived by our analysis from another recorded fact |
| 20 | `analyzer`, `auto`, `borrowed` | a heuristic, or a source this table does not know |

## Semantics

`outranks(new_set_by, existing_set_by)` — Whether a write by `new_set_by` may replace a fact from `existing_set_by`.

It compares with `>=`, so **an equal rank replaces**. That is deliberate:
a later `auto` pass must be able to improve on an earlier one, and an
analyst must be able to correct their own earlier edit. The rule is about
provenance rank, not immutability.

`set_by_priority(set_by)` — Rank of a `set_by` string. Unknown and empty rank as `auto`.

An unrecognised or empty string therefore ranks at `20`, the same rank
as `auto` — neither zero nor the top. Ranking an unknown source lowest
would let a typo be permanently outranked by everything; ranking it
highest would let a typo clobber real debug information.

The ranks are compared across versions of this code against rows written
by older ones, so the numbers are frozen: renumbering a rung silently
re-decides precedence questions already settled in shipped project files.

## Who enforces it

`outranks` is imported by `python/glaurung/llm/kb/xref_db.py` and
`python/glaurung/llm/kb/type_db.py`, and every setter that writes a named
fact calls it before the write. There is no caller-side bypass: the guard
is inside the setter, not at the call site.

```
rg -n 'outranks\(' python/glaurung/llm/kb/
```

`python/tests/test_kb_provenance_rank.py` pins the ranking and
`python/tests/test_kb_manual_precedence.py` pins the top rung against
every setter.

<!-- prose:start -->

## Why the ladder looks like this

Provenance is not a Glaurung invention, and the interesting comparison is not
"do the incumbents have it" — they do — but *where each of them enforces it*.

**Ghidra** has the closest analogue: `SourceType` is a five-constant priority
lattice (`DEFAULT` 1 < `ANALYSIS` 2 = `AI` 2 < `IMPORTED` 3 < `USER_DEFINED` 4).
But `SymbolDB.doSetNameAndNamespace` never compares the incoming `SourceType`
against the stored one; the only gate in the setter is default/non-default, and
real enforcement lives in scattered caller sites. A plugin that calls
`symbol.setName(x, SourceType.ANALYSIS)` overwrites a `USER_DEFINED` name
without complaint. Ghidra had to retrofit priority comparison onto value
equality — commit GP-6008, *"Changed SourceType examination to base upon
priority instead of specific value equality when appropriate."* Ghidra comments
also carry no provenance at all: `CodeUnit.setComment` takes no `SourceType`.

**IDA** is two-valued — user versus auto, behind `has_user_name()` /
`has_auto_name()`. It cannot tell you whether a stored name came from DWARF, a
FLIRT signature, a PDB, or propagation. **Binary Ninja** carries a numeric
confidence that composes multiplicatively rather than a flat enum. **angr** has
no general model: one enum for prototypes, and `SimVariable.renamed` means
"has a non-default name" rather than "a human set this", because four of its
seven writers are automatic.

Two design consequences follow, and both are visible in the table above.

**The enforcement point is the setter, not the caller.** `outranks` is called
inside `set_function_name`, `set_comment`, `set_data_label`,
`set_function_prototype` and the type-DB writers, so no caller — analyst, CLI,
LLM tool, or indexing pass — can bypass it by forgetting to check. That is the
one structural difference from Ghidra's shape, and it is the reason the
vocabulary in the table can be trusted to mean what it says.

**Ties are stated, not invented.** `dwarf`, `pdb` and `gopclntab` are the same
class of evidence on three platforms; nothing in the tree can order them, and
inventing an order would be a decision with no basis, so they share rank 80.
`flirt` and `cil` share 50 for the same reason.

## Why `borrowed` sits with the heuristics

`borrowed` names a fact copied from a *different* binary judged similar — the
only source whose subject is not this binary at all, and on the face of it the
weakest thing recorded. It nonetheless sits at parity with `auto` and
`analyzer` rather than below them, because what borrowing overwrites is a
synthesised `sub_1234` placeholder written by the discovery pass, and a real
name transferred from a matched function carries strictly more information than
a placeholder. Ranked one rung lower, `borrow_symbols` cannot write at all and
the feature silently does nothing;
`python/tests/test_borrow_symbols.py::test_borrow_lifts_stripped_target_naming`
is the test that catches it.

Ghidra reached the identical question when it added AI-sourced markup: it added
a `Speculative` rung below analysis, reverted it a day later, and shipped the
new source at parity with `ANALYSIS` instead. Parity is the defensible answer.
A rung nothing can ever climb out of is not a rung.

`borrowed` still cannot touch `flirt`, `stdlib`, real debug information, or the
analyst, which is what the ladder was needed for.

## Rank is not a lock

Rank answers *"which fact wins"*. It does not answer *"may the analysis
re-derive this at all"*. Those are different questions, and Ghidra needs both
`SourceType` **and** separate `namelock` / `typelock` bits because of it. We
have only the first, and the gap is worth knowing before copying the design in
either direction — Ghidra's locks are not stored, they are recomputed on every
decompile, and for parameters partly by string prefix, so an analyst who names
a parameter `param_count` silently loses its namelock.

## Undo captures the manual rung only

`_record_undo` in `python/glaurung/llm/kb/xref_db.py` returns immediately for
any `set_by` other than `manual`. The reasoning is that an automatic write can
be re-derived by re-running the pass that produced it, so undoing one is
meaningless — the next index would put it back. A manual write encodes analyst
intent that nothing else can recover, which is what `glaurung undo` exists to
protect.

## Reading the tag

`set_by` is a column, not an internal flag, so every surface that lists named
entities can print it and several do — `glaurung find` appends `(set_by=…)` to
function and type rows, and `glaurung rename` / `comment` / `label` / `proto`
report the holding provenance when a write is refused. The uniform, queryable
store is the part of this that is genuinely a differentiator: the analyst and
the LLM agent write through the same ranked column, and either can ask which
facts are trustworthy and which are guesses.
